note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md (2026-11-28). Wide pictures only (1920x1088). Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper 60% of the frame, clear of the word box. God and the angels are not pictured; Abraham, Sarah, Lot, Hagar, Abimelech and the others are only ordinary people of today, seen from behind, small, or as hands. Fixed recurring objects: the town of Sodom is a walled town of plain flat-roofed pale stone houses with a heavy timber gate, no church, no dome, no steeple and no tower of any kind; the pillar of salt is a single tall pillar of rough white crystalline salt, taller than a person, standing alone on a barren plain. Kept tasteful: the mob and the daughters' scenes are shown only by a shut door, a night street, an old man alone and the two nations' beginnings.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning; (2) write picture ideas for each; (3) judge them; (4) make the top two for each slot as real pictures and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: Two travelers come to Sodom at evening; Lot welcomes them in, the men of the city surround his house, and the men inside strike them blind.
Lot is told to bring his family out before the city is ruined; he lingers, they take his hand and lead him out, and he asks to flee to a small city.
Fire falls on the cities of the plain; Lot's wife looks back and becomes salt; Abraham sees the smoke at dawn, and God remembers him.
Lot lives afraid in a cave in the hills; his daughters bear Moab and Ben-Ammi.
